final.summary: Outfall pH stayed near neutral through the treatment interval, showing no raw alkaline discharge reached the outfall. Outfall flow was elevated while conductivity was depressed over the same stretch, indicating added low-conductivity water at the outfall. ETP inflow is missing for most of the interval, so it cannot be shown that the batch water passed through the ETP or that the extra outfall flow was treated effluent.

explanations.label: Normal operation: batch wastewater treated through ETP
Bypass around ETP discharging untreated water
ETP stopped with tank overflow untreated
Aeration cut (low power) with flow passing through

key_evidence.why: Outfall pH stayed near neutral with no reading above 9, so no raw alkaline water reached the outfall.
Outfall flow was elevated compared with outside the window, suggesting extra water at the outfall.
Conductivity was depressed during the same elevated-flow stretch, consistent with low-conductivity water added.
ETP inflow has no readings for most of the treatment interval, so flow through the ETP cannot be checked.
Tank level stayed mid-range and never filled, showing no overflow during the S2 gap.
Power stayed in a normal range, showing aeration load was present.
Power feed does not repeat another day, so it is not a replayed feed.

final.scope_line: Based on flow, power, pH and conductivity records for 2026-10-13 14:00 to 2026-10-14 18:00. Does not measure every pollutant.
limitations: ETP inflow missing for most of the treatment interval, so tank, ETP and boundary balances cannot be computed.
Power-versus-load check cannot be computed without inflow coverage.
No lab BOD result and no meter photos are available to confirm treatment performance.
Logbook claim of normal operation is a factory claim, not physical evidence.
Conductivity and flow alone cannot separate added groundwater from a flow meter error without the missing inflow record.

result.note: ETP balance: treated flow reaching the outfall vs outfall flow (same time). Boundary balance: intake vs outfall + losses + sludge water + tank storage change (reuse cancels). Tank balance: wastewater arriving (estimated from intake) vs ETP inflow + storage change; unaccounted water left the tank another way, or was intake water that never became wastewater. null means a required signal is under 80% coverage.
